metadata.title: Kim Valles Personal Training Program
metadata.purpose: Kim's actual current training program — the gold standard reference for TRAIN. When a client profile closely matches Kim's (intermediate-advanced female, body recomp, upper/lower split, full gym, 4 days/week), this program serves as the primary blueprint. Claude personalizes from this foundation rather than building from scratch.
metadata.goal: Body Recomposition — simultaneous fat loss and muscle gain
metadata.coach_note: This is my program. Built around my goal, my body, and what I know works. If you're similar to me — intermediate, recomp-focused, love training lower body — this is your closest blueprint. We personalize from here.

weekly_volume_summary.description: Verified sets per muscle group per week — cross-referenced against programming_variables.json targets

glutes.status: Elite — primary focus of this program
glutes.note: Above maximum adaptive volume — intentional. Glutes are the priority. Program is designed around maximizing glute development.

back.status: Strong — vertical and horizontal pulls balanced

chest.status: At minimum effective volume — adequate for recomp

shoulders.status: Strong — front, side, and rear delt covered

biceps.status: Good — intensity exceeds volume on paper (failure sets with static holds)
biceps.execution_note: Kim trains biceps to true failure with peak contraction static holds — RPE 9-10 every set. Effective stimulus is higher than set count suggests.

calves.status: Strong — split across both lower days

core.status: High intensity circuit — quality over quantity
core.note: Core circuit is advanced superset format. Sled pushes and battle ropes demand significant core stability. Supplemented with weekly hot pilates or active movement session.

split_structure.day_5: Active Recovery — Hot Pilates or intentional movement
split_structure.periodization_style: Daily Undulating — Day 2 is strength focused (4-6 reps), Day 4 is hypertrophy/tension focused (higher reps, supersets, drop sets)
split_structure.programming_philosophy: Lower body days are heavy and volume-focused. Upper body alternates between strength stimulus and metabolic tension. Conditioning finishers (sled, battle ropes, cardio) support fat loss without sacrificing muscle.

day_1.name: Day 1 — Glutes & Lower Body
day_1.focus: Glute dominant — hip hinge and isolation priority

key_exercises: World's Greatest Stretch — 5 reps per side

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Drive
exercises.variation: Full drive, pulses, static hold — all within same set
exercises.cue: Drive through heels. Full squeeze at top — hold it. Pulses keep tension constant. Static hold is peak contraction — breathe through it.
exercises.kim_note: This is the anchor of the whole session. Load it heavy. The triple variation (full, pulse, static) creates massive glute stimulus in one exercise.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift — Glute Focused
exercises.cue: Push hips back, not down. Feel the glute stretch at the bottom — that's where growth happens. Drive hips forward at the top, squeeze hard.
exercises.kim_note: Glute-focused means deliberately pushing hips back further than a standard RDL. Slow eccentric is everything here.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Weaker leg first — match reps exactly. Torso slight forward lean to bias glutes. Lower straight down, drive through front heel.
exercises.kim_note: One of the best exercises in the program. Don't rush it.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl — Single Leg Lying
exercises.cue: Slow on the way down — that's where the muscle grows. Curl to full range. Squeeze the hamstring at peak contraction.
exercises.kim_note: Single leg keeps both sides honest. The 3-second eccentric is non-negotiable.

exercises.name: Glute Medius Kickbacks
exercises.cue: Feel the outside of the glute. Keep hips square — don't rotate. Full range, squeeze at end.
exercises.kim_note: Glute medius work is what creates that rounded shape on the outside of the glute. Don't skip this.

exercises.name: Calf Raises
exercises.cue: Full range — all the way up, all the way down. Pause at bottom for a stretch. 2-second pause at top.

exercises.name: Core Circuit
exercises.format: 3 supersets — complete all 6 exercises as a circuit, rest 60s, repeat
exercises.kim_note: This circuit is genuinely hard. Don't underestimate it. By round 3 you should be fighting. That's the point.

day_2.name: Day 2 — Upper Body 1 (Strength Focused)
day_2.focus: Strength stimulus — heavier loads, lower reps, longer rest
day_2.programming_note: Day 2 is the strength day of the DUP rotation. Heavier loads, 6-8 rep ranges on primary movements. This is where we build the foundation that Day 4 will refine.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Core braced. Don't arch the lower back. Press overhead — full lockout at top.
exercises.kim_note: This is the strength anchor of upper day 1. Load it.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Ups
exercises.variation: 2 sets close grip + 2 sets wide grip
exercises.cue: Initiate from the lats — not the arms. Drive elbows to hips. Full range — dead hang at bottom, chin over bar at top.
exercises.kim_note: Close grip hits biceps and lower lats more. Wide grip hits upper lats and creates width. Alternating both in one session is smart programming.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Chest Press
exercises.cue: Lower to upper chest — feel the stretch. Press up and slightly in. 3-second eccentric is the work.
exercises.kim_note: 4 sets here — this is the chest volume anchor for the week.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.cue: Elbows wide and flared — this targets upper back and rear delts. Squeeze hard at top. Control the descent.
exercises.kim_note: Wide grip T-bar is one of the best upper back exercises. The elbow flare is what makes it different from a standard row.

exercises.name: Lateral Raises
exercises.cue: Lead with elbows, not hands. Slight forward lean. Feel the lateral head of the shoulder — not the traps.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Pull to upper chest. Feel the lats — not the arms. Slight lean back.

exercises.name: Tricep Extensions
exercises.cue: Keep elbows locked in place — only the forearms move. Full extension at bottom.

exercises.name: Seated Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curls
exercises.reps: To failure with static holds at peak contraction
exercises.execution_note: These are NOT standard sets. Curl to peak contraction — hold for 2 seconds squeezing hard. Lower slow. Go to true failure. RPE 9-10 every set.
exercises.kim_note: The incline position stretches the long head of the bicep at the bottom — this is what makes this variation so effective. Static holds at peak contraction add time under tension beyond what the reps suggest.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Neutral grip — thumbs up. Keep elbows pinned at sides. Full range.
exercises.kim_note: Added to bring bicep weekly volume to 8 sets and hit the brachialis — the muscle under the bicep that adds thickness and peak.

cardio_finisher.name: Treadmill — 1 Mile
cardio_finisher.protocol: Incline 12 — alternating speed 3 walking and speed 6 running
cardio_finisher.purpose: Conditioning and caloric expenditure without compromising muscle recovery
cardio_finisher.kim_note: This incline protocol hits glutes and hamstrings hard even on an upper body day. It's efficient — cardiovascular and body recomp in one.

day_3.name: Day 3 — Quads & Lower Body 2
day_3.focus: Quad dominant with hamstring and posterior chain support

key_exercises: World's Greatest Stretch — 5 reps per side

exercises.name: Goblet Squat — Drop Set
exercises.reps: 8-10 then drop weight and continue to failure
exercises.cue: Sit deep into the squat — chest tall, elbows inside knees. Drop set means no rest between weights — immediately reduce load and keep going.
exercises.kim_note: Drop sets on squats are brutal. This is a quad and glute burner in one. Don't shortchange the depth.

exercises.name: Straight Leg RDL
exercises.cue: Legs straighter than a standard RDL — feel a deep hamstring stretch at the bottom. Keep back flat. Drive hips through at top.
exercises.kim_note: This is the hamstring anchor of Day 3. The straight leg position maximizes the hamstring stretch — this is what drives growth.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunges
exercises.cue: Step back — lower straight down. Front knee stays behind toes. Drive through front heel to stand.
exercises.kim_note: Reverse lunge puts less stress on the knee than forward lunge — better for most people and just as effective.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.cue: Feet hip width or slightly wider. Don't lock out knees at top — keep constant tension. Control the descent.
exercises.kim_note: Leg press after lunges and squats adds volume without the balance demand. Load it — quads should be burning.

exercises.name: Single Leg Extensions
exercises.cue: Extend to full lockout — squeeze the quad hard at the top. 3-second slow lowering. Single leg keeps both sides equal.
exercises.kim_note: Single leg over bilateral — eliminates dominant leg compensation. The slow eccentric here is key.

exercises.name: Hyperextensions
exercises.cue: Hinge at the hip — not the lower back. Feel the glute and hamstring doing the work. Don't hyperextend at the top.
exercises.kim_note: Great posterior chain finisher. Protects the lower back by strengthening the erectors.

exercises.name: Calf Raises
exercises.cue: Full range. Pause at bottom for stretch. 2-second squeeze at top.
exercises.kim_note: Added to Day 3 — brings weekly calf volume to 8 sets total. Calves need frequency to grow.

conditioning_finisher.name: Sled Pushes
conditioning_finisher.purpose: Power, conditioning, and caloric expenditure. Demands full lower body and core engagement.
conditioning_finisher.kim_note: Sled pushes are a full body conditioning finisher disguised as a leg exercise. Drive from the hips and legs. Stay low. This is where you leave everything.

day_4.name: Day 4 — Upper Body 2 (Hypertrophy & Tension)
day_4.focus: Higher reps, supersets, drop sets — metabolic stress and time under tension
day_4.programming_note: This is the hypertrophy and tension day of the DUP rotation. Higher reps, shorter rest, superset pairings. The goal is metabolic stress and muscle damage — different stimulus from Day 2 strength work.

exercises.name: Lateral Raises — Drop Set
exercises.reps: 10-12 then drop and continue to failure
exercises.cue: Lead with elbows. Feel the lateral head burning by the drop set. No rest between weight drops.
exercises.kim_note: Starting with lateral raises drop sets pre-fatigues the delts for everything that follows. Smart sequencing.

exercises.name: Upright Rear Delt Row
exercises.cue: Elbows drive up and out — not straight up. Feel the rear delt and upper trap engaging.
exercises.kim_note: Rear delt work is essential for shoulder health and posture. Never skip.

exercises.name: SUPERSET A — Close Grip Chest Press + Diamond Push-Up
Close Grip Chest Press
exercises.cue: Hands closer than shoulder width. Lower to mid-chest. Feel the inner chest and triceps working together.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up — Bodyweight
exercises.cue: Hands in diamond shape. Lower all the way to the floor. Push to full extension. Go until you genuinely cannot do one more.

exercises.kim_note: Close grip press into immediate diamond push-ups to failure — chest and triceps are completely fried after this superset. That's exactly the point.

exercises.name: SUPERSET B — Seated Row + Single Arm Lat Pulldown
Seated Row or Low Row Machine
exercises.cue: Drive elbows back. Squeeze shoulder blades together at end. Control the return.

exercises.name: Single Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Pull to upper chest. Feel the lat stretching at the top — full range. Single arm exposes any imbalance.

exercises.kim_note: Horizontal pull into vertical pull — hits the lats from two different angles back to back. Back gets completely saturated.

exercises.name: SUPERSET C — Seated Dips Machine + Seated Incline DB Bicep Curls
Seated Dips Machine
exercises.cue: Full extension at bottom. Control the return. Feel the tricep doing the work — not the chest.

exercises.name: Seated Incline DB Bicep Curls — To Failure
exercises.execution_note: Go to true failure. Static hold at peak contraction for 2 seconds every rep. By the last rep you should have nothing left.
exercises.cue: The incline stretches the long head — feel it at the bottom. Curl to peak, hold, lower slow. That last rep should be a fight.

exercises.kim_note: Triceps and biceps superset — antagonist pairing means one rests while the other works. Ends with biceps to absolute failure. Arms are completely done after this.

conditioning_finisher.name: Battle Ropes
conditioning_finisher.variations: Alternating waves, double waves, slams, circles — mix throughout
conditioning_finisher.purpose: High-intensity conditioning, caloric expenditure, grip and core endurance
conditioning_finisher.kim_note: Battle ropes after this upper body session is savage. Arms are already fatigued — the ropes finish the job. 20 on, 40 off keeps intensity maximal every round.

day_5.name: Day 5 — Active Recovery
day_5.focus: Intentional movement — nervous system recovery, mobility, enjoyment
day_5.note: Day 5 is not optional rest — it's active recovery. The difference matters. You're not doing nothing. You're moving with intention at a lower intensity.

option_A.name: Hot Pilates
option_A.description: Kim's preferred active recovery. Heat + pilates = mobility, core, and nervous system reset in one session. Counts as a full active recovery day.
option_A.kim_note: Hot pilates is the perfect complement to this program — it hits everything the strength training doesn't. Core stability, hip mobility, thoracic rotation, balance. Plus the heat speeds up recovery. This is my weekly reset.

option_B.name: Intentional Movement — Client's Choice
option_B.description: Any low-intensity activity the client genuinely enjoys for 30-45 minutes.
examples: Stretch and mobility session at home
Any movement that feels good to your body today
option_B.intensity: Conversational pace — you should be able to hold a full conversation
option_B.kim_note: The only rule is that it's something you actually want to do. Active recovery works best when it doesn't feel like a workout. Move your body in a way that feels like a gift, not an obligation.

day_5.what_not_to_do: No heavy lifting. No high-intensity cardio. No training to failure. This day exists to clear fatigue so Days 1-4 next week are powerful.

how_claude_uses_this_program.primary_use: When a client matches Kim's profile — intermediate to advanced female, body recomp goal, 4 days/week, full gym — use this as the primary blueprint
personalization_steps: Keep the split structure — Day 1 lower glute, Day 2 upper strength, Day 3 lower quad, Day 4 upper hypertrophy
Adjust exercise selection for client's specific equipment if different
Apply injury modifications from injury_navigation.json if needed
Scale volume to client's experience — reduce sets for beginner-intermediate
Adjust conditioning finishers based on client's cardio preference and goal
Replace hot pilates with client's preferred active recovery activity
Write program notes in Kim's voice referencing the client's identity statement and vision
how_claude_uses_this_program.do_not_copy_verbatim: This is Kim's program — personalize for every client. The structure is the blueprint, not the prescription.

progression_guide.week_1_to_2: Establish the movements. Learn the feel of each exercise. RPE should feel like 7-8 — hard but controlled.
progression_guide.week_3: Add weight where RIR allows on all primary compound movements. Push RPE to 8-9 on primary lifts.
progression_guide.week_4: Deload — reduce all sets by 40%, maintain load. Same movements, lower volume.
progression_guide.week_5_new_mesocycle: New baseline above week 1. Add 1 set to primary compounds across Day 1 and Day 3.
progression_guide.ongoing: Progressive overload is non-negotiable. Track weights. Beat last week by at least one rep or 2.5 lbs somewhere every session.
